contract.topic: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and the Power Iteration

required_items.canonical_statement: For A in R^{n x n}, a non-zero vector v is an eigenvector when Av=lambda v; lambda is its associated eigenvalue. The non-zero condition is essential.
conditions: A is a real n by n matrix.
v is non-zero.
prohibited_drift: Do not allow the zero vector as an eigenvector carrying eigenvalue information.
Do not interchange the roles of v and lambda.

required_items.canonical_statement: For a real symmetric matrix A=A^T, the spectral theorem supplies an orthonormal basis of real eigenvectors, giving A=Q Lambda Q^T and representing every x as a sum of eigenvector components with c_i=v_i^T x.
conditions: A is real and symmetric.
Q has eigenvectors as columns and is orthogonal.
prohibited_drift: Do not claim this orthogonal real decomposition for arbitrary non-symmetric matrices.
Preserve the coefficient relation c_i=v_i^T x.

required_items.canonical_statement: The eigenvalues are ordered by magnitude as |lambda_1|>|lambda_2|>=...>=|lambda_n|, so lambda_1 is unique in magnitude and is the dominant eigenvalue.
conditions: The strict first inequality is required for a unique dominant magnitude.
prohibited_drift: Do not replace largest magnitude with largest algebraic value.
Do not weaken the strict dominant-gap condition when stating the convergence result.

required_items.canonical_statement: Starting from a non-zero x_0, power iteration computes y_{k+1}=Ax_k and normalises x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}/||y_{k+1}||_2; normalisation controls scale without changing direction.
conditions: x_0 is non-zero.
The normalising denominator is non-zero.
prohibited_drift: Do not omit normalisation from the displayed update rule.
Do not describe normalisation as changing the iterate direction.

required_items.canonical_statement: Under the symmetric eigenbasis expansion, A^k x_0 separates the dominant term lambda_1^k c_1 v_1 from terms scaled by (lambda_i/lambda_1)^k; a non-zero c_1 and a strict magnitude gap make the subordinate ratios vanish.
conditions: A is in the real symmetric setting with the stated eigenbasis.
c_1=v_1^T x_0 is non-zero.
|lambda_1|>|lambda_2|.
prohibited_drift: Do not drop the initial projection condition.
Do not claim all components vanish without the magnitude comparison.

required_items.canonical_statement: For a real symmetric matrix, a unique dominant magnitude, non-zero initial projection onto v_1, and no zero Ax_k iterate imply that direction error generally decreases asymptotically at a rate governed by |lambda_2/lambda_1|^k.
conditions: A is real and symmetric.
|lambda_1|>|lambda_2|.
The initial vector has non-zero projection onto v_1.
No iterate produces Ax_k=0.
prohibited_drift: Do not state convergence without all three listed assumptions.
Do not turn the generally asymptotic rate into an unconditional finite-iteration error bound.

required_items.canonical_statement: When lambda_1<0, successive normalised iterates may alternate sign; this is not failure because v_1 and -v_1 describe the same eigendirection.
conditions: The dominant eigenvalue is negative.
prohibited_drift: Do not interpret sign alternation alone as failure to converge in direction.
Do not identify v_1 and -v_1 as different eigendirections.

required_items.canonical_statement: The Rayleigh quotient rho(x_k)=x_k^T A x_k/(x_k^T x_k), reducing to x_k^T A x_k for a normalised vector, estimates lambda_1 as x_k approaches v_1 for symmetric A.
conditions: x_k is non-zero for the quotient.
The convergence-to-lambda_1 statement uses a symmetric matrix and x_k approaching v_1.
prohibited_drift: Do not use the simplified quotient for an unnormalised vector without its denominator.
Do not claim the quotient targets the dominant eigenvalue under conditions not stated in the source.

required_items.canonical_statement: The eigenpair residual is r_k=Ax_k-rho(x_k)x_k; an exact eigenpair has zero residual, and ||r_k||_2 is a meaningful computational stopping measure because vector differences can be distorted by sign flips.
conditions: rho(x_k) is the Rayleigh quotient used with x_k.
prohibited_drift: Do not replace the residual test with only successive-vector similarity.
Do not omit the sign ambiguity when interpreting vector differences.

required_items.canonical_statement: The stated algorithm normalises x_0, applies matrix-vector multiplication and normalisation, checks breakdown, computes the Rayleigh estimate and residual, stops when the residual norm is at most epsilon, and otherwise stops after K iterations.
conditions: x_0 is non-zero.
epsilon is positive.
K is the maximum iteration count.
prohibited_drift: Do not move the breakdown check after division by ||y||_2.
Do not remove either the residual tolerance stop or the maximum-iteration fallback.

required_items.canonical_statement: If v_1^T x_0=0, the initial vector has no dominant eigendirection component, exact arithmetic cannot create it, and power iteration will not converge to v_1.
conditions: The dominant eigenvector is v_1 and the initial projection is exactly zero.
prohibited_drift: Do not imply that repeated multiplication creates a missing exact eigencomponent.
Do not treat this case as ordinary slow convergence to v_1.

required_items.canonical_statement: If the two largest eigenvalue magnitudes are equal, a unique eigenvector need not be selected; if their ratio is close to one while still separated, convergence can be very slow.
conditions: The equal-magnitude case has |lambda_1|=|lambda_2|.
The slow-convergence case has |lambda_2/lambda_1| close to one.
prohibited_drift: Do not conflate non-unique dominance with merely slow convergence.
Do not promise a unique eigenvector when the dominant magnitude is repeated.

required_items.canonical_statement: Power iteration targets the eigenvalue of largest magnitude, not necessarily the most positive eigenvalue; between 5 and -8, -8 is dominant by magnitude.
conditions: Eigenvalues are compared by absolute value.
prohibited_drift: Do not describe the target as the largest algebraic eigenvalue.
Preserve the negative example's conclusion.

conditional_items.canonical_statement: Eigenvalues are roots of det(A-lambda I)=0; for large matrices, iterative matrix-vector products are presented as a preferable numerical strategy to explicitly forming the characteristic polynomial.
conditions: I is the identity matrix of compatible dimension.
prohibited_drift: Do not replace the characteristic equation with a different determinant convention without review.
Do not present the iterative-strategy statement as an exact algebraic equivalence.

conditional_items.canonical_statement: Although power iteration applies to some non-symmetric matrices, the clean orthogonal decomposition is not generally available; defective matrices, complex dominant eigenvalues, and non-normal behaviour require additional care and are outside these notes' scope.
conditions: The core convergence explanation is restricted to the real symmetric setting.
prohibited_drift: Do not generalise the symmetric proof or convergence claim to all non-symmetric matrices.

conditional_items.canonical_statement: The Python implementation converts A and x0 to floating NumPy arrays, requires A to be square and x0 to have compatible one-dimensional shape, rejects a zero initial vector, and normalises x before iteration.
conditions: NumPy is available.
A and x0 can be converted to floating arrays.
prohibited_drift: Do not remove the square-matrix, dimension, or non-zero-initial-vector checks.
Do not silently change the stated exception behaviour.

conditional_items.canonical_statement: Generated implementations must validate that max_iterations is a positive integer before entering the iteration loop. Invalid values must raise a clear ValueError. For valid values, preserve the source iteration, breakdown check, normalization, residual stopping test, maximum-iteration fallback, and four-value return structure.
conditions: The iteration range is 1 through max_iterations inclusive.
The returned tuple is (eigenvalue, x, residual_norm, iteration count).
prohibited_drift: Do not divide by a zero y norm before raising the breakdown error.
Do not change the residual-based early return or the four-value return structure.

conditional_items.canonical_statement: For A=[[4,1],[1,2]] with x0=(1,1), the exact eigenvalues are 3+sqrt(2) and 3-sqrt(2); the implementation should estimate the dominant value 3+sqrt(2) and produce a small residual.
conditions: The implementation is run with the supplied initial vector and default parameters.
prohibited_drift: Do not identify 3-sqrt(2) as the dominant eigenvalue for this matrix.
Do not treat a small residual as requiring a particular sign of the eigenvector.
